Both sites are within a protected area, the Bosque Protector Cordillera del Cóndor, and are within 100 m of the international border between Ecuador and Peru. The Cordillera del Cóndor crest in this region, at about 2000 – 2400 m elevation, is composed of flat-topped table mountains of the Hollín sandstone formation.

children.name: Nothodissotis alenensis Ver.-Lib. & O.Lachenaud
children.description: Description. Deciduous shrub, 1.5 - 2.5 m tall; stems glabrous except for strigillose pubescence at the nodes; internodes short, 15 - 80 mm long (Fig. 5 A). Leaves simple, opposite, petiole 8 - 17 mm long with appressed pubescence; blades elliptic, 50 - 95 x 15 - 30 mm, base obtuse, apex acute, margins minutely serrulate, hairs appressed on both sides, longitudinal nerves 3 (5) from the base, somewhat prominent adaxially, strongly so abaxially and with simple appressed pubescence (Fig. 5 B, C).

children.name: Nothodissotis barteri
children.description: Distribution and habitat. Nothodissotis barteri is sparsely distributed in Cameroon (Ebo forest), south-eastern Equatorial Guinea (near Nsork), northern Gabon, and Principe Island (Fig. 4). It occurs exclusively on rock outcrops at 370 - 1000 m elevation, mainly in low shrubby vegetation near the edge of the rocks (" manteau arbustif ") where it is locally dominant, and sometimes also as isolated plants in rocky grassland dominated by Afrotrilepis pilosa (Boeck.) J. Raynal (Cyperaceae).
